notes: DAX is the functional auxiliary nonce form and MIP is the lexical-adjective nonce form in this draft. Counterbalance nonce forms across morphosyntactic conditions in the final experiment. Context components that can appear first in an order variant introduce the participant by name rather than with an ungrounded pronoun; pronouns are retained later where their antecedent is clear.
Context-only and whole-scenario norming must use the same context wording/order for a given item version. Whole-scenario norming differs only by appending the familiar-English target sentence.

For test/filler items, three order-pair types are balanced exactly: P1=N-E-D + E-D-N; P2=D-N-E + N-D-E; P3=E-N-D + D-E-N. Each pair occurs 8 times, and each of the six individual three-part orders therefore occurs 8 times.
For training items, each root/deontic candidate has N-D and D-N versions; each epistemic candidate has N-E and E-N versions. The untrained flavor is not made false during training.

Training candidate syntax is balanced 4/4/4 per flavor across Declarative, Wh-question, and Yes/no inversion. Critical test and filler targets remain declarative to keep the flavor-transfer judgment syntactically conservative. Norming practice/example trials should be declarative.

E_status records whether the target proposition is epistemically possible (E+) or ruled out (E-). epistemic_support_type separately records HOW E+ is established: explicit live alternatives/positive evidence versus merely remaining open because nothing rules it out. Both receive 'Yes' to the context-only epistemic possibility question because both are compatible with the information state.
